mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in unemployment rate below 6% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 6% but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 5 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment is low and the Federal Funds rate is high, it may indicate tightening monetary policy, leading to negative equity returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive over the 60-day horizon more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, lower Federal Funds rates reduce borrowing costs, potentially boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are low but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests higher economic output, which may lead to positive equity returns as companies increase production and potentially earnings.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive equity returns as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If HOUST exceeds 900 but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 5 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real federal funds rate adjusted consumer spending, combined with low Federal Funds rates, may indicate a positive economic environment for equities.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is positive and FEDFUNDS are low but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a low unemployment rate may signal an overheating economy, leading to potential negative equity returns as the market anticipates a slowdown.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low in a late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 returns are positive over the 60-day horizon more than 30% of the time.
